Thought: To synthesize a tertiary amide from a carboxylic acid chloride, we need to react it with a suitable amine. A tertiary amide is formed when a carboxylic acid chloride reacts with a secondary amine. This is because a secondary amine has two carbon-containing groups and one hydrogen attached to the nitrogen, allowing it to form a new N-C bond to the carbonyl carbon of the carboxylic acid chloride. A primary amine would form a secondary amide, and a tertiary amine cannot form a stable amide bond as it lacks a hydrogen to form the amide. Ammonia would form a primary amide.
